subject: Civic Education
lesson: Explains the importance of fulfilling the duties of rights of child: Institutional Fact-Finding Station: Competency Level 8.2.2
unique_learning_outcome: Explains the importance of fulfilling the duties of rights of child.
Expresses how enjoying rights of child bring about child development.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: Teacher explains that Sri Lanka has ratified United Nations Convention on Rights of Child, emphasizing children's right to education, health facilities, security, participation in decision-making processes, development opportunities, existence without exploitation and freedom from child labor.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Teacher explains the scenario: 'A parent is struggling with childcare duties due to work commitments. They need help finding solutions.', assigns roles (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary), and distributes fact-finding station materials.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students inspect surrounding area for potential institutions that can support this child's situation, record evidence on the chart paper

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Teacher circulates across teams to facilitate role execution and formatively check progress.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students continue exploring institutions, record findings on chart paper

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: Teacher facilitates team presentations to share their discoveries and insights.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Teams present findings; peers critique each other's work

summary: Teacher and students synthesize core findings, reinforcing key civic competencies and takeaways.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Teacher assesses student understanding through presentation and peer review, checks for connections to the Convention on Rights of Child.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Five-minute in-class assignment: Each student writes two key responsibilities on their reflection sheet.
selected_activity:
Activity: Institutional Fact-Finding Station: Competency Level 8.2.2
Approach: Students use institutional fact-finding station to explore 'Explains the importance of fulfilling the duties of rights of child.'. Students inspect the provided scenario or accessible surroundings, record evidence, and compare findings. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Student task: Students inspect the provided scenario or accessible surroundings, record evidence, and compare findings. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Teacher facilitation: Organizes all 40 students using 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. and monitors progress with outcome-focused prompts and time checks. Circulates across 8 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress.
Expected output: An evidence record with one supported conclusion.
Grouping: 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
